title: Blueberry Cream Cheese Stuffed French Toast
changes_from_base: The bread is stuffed with a cream cheese and blueberry jam spread, then dipped in a thin egg, flour and water batter rather than a milk custard, so the outside fries up crisp.
summary: Toasted sandwiches filled with a sweet blueberry and cream cheese mixture, golden outside and ready for a syrup drizzle.

ingredients.item: slices good white sandwich bread (about 280 g)

steps.title: Mix filling
steps.text: Stir together 113 g cream cheese, 1 tbsp caster sugar, 2 tbsp blueberry jam and ¼ tsp cinnamon until smooth.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Divide the mixture between 4 bread slices and top each with a second slice to close the sandwiches.

steps.title: Batter
steps.text: Whisk 1 egg, 240 ml cold water, 65 g plain flour and 1 tsp vanilla in a shallow dish until the batter runs smoothly off a spoon.

steps.title: First pan
steps.text: Melt half of the 56 g butter in a large non-stick pan, coat two sandwiches briefly in the batter and fry until the crust turns a deep gold, roughly 3 min a side.

steps.title: Second pan
steps.text: Add the rest of the butter to the pan and fry the remaining sandwiches the same way.

steps.title: Plate
steps.text: Cut each sandwich into triangles and serve while hot, with 60 ml maple syrup poured over.

tips: Use jam straight from the jar so the filling spreads easily without extra stirring.
Fry in two batches so the pan stays hot enough to give a crisp crust each time.
Serve as soon as they're cooked, while the filling is still soft and warm.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Eat fresh for the best texture; leftovers can be covered and kept in the fridge for a day, then reheated gently in a pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
